lane.name: Bluegrass, old-time, and newgrass
lane.definition: Alison Krauss, Nickel Creek, Punch Brothers, Billy Strings, Molly Tuttle, Sierra Ferrell: the bluegrass line as its own tradition.

albums.label: Starday Records
albums.description: The debut of the band that named 'newgrass,' fusing traditional bluegrass instrumentation (banjo, mandolin, fiddle) with rock and jazz-influenced improvisation and a hippie-era openness to extended jamming. It broke from bluegrass orthodoxy's strict traditionalism far more aggressively than most contemporaries. It is for hearing bluegrass's founding progressive-jam experiment, decades before Billy Strings.
albums.lineage: Descends from first-generation bluegrass (Bill Monroe, the Stanley Brothers; R1) but breaks from its strict traditionalism; its improvisational, genre-blending path seems to lead to Nickel Creek, Punch Brothers and Billy Strings.

albums.label: Sugar Hill
albums.description: Produced by Alison Krauss, the trio's breakout album mixes bluegrass virtuosity (Chris Thile's mandolin, Sara Watkins's fiddle) with pop songcraft and progressive instrumental stretches. It introduced bluegrass technique to a younger, indie-adjacent audience far from the genre's traditional base. It is for hearing the record that launched Chris Thile's push to blend bluegrass virtuosity with art-music ambition.
albums.lineage: Sounds like a newgrass descendant of New Grass Revival's genre-blending example, filtered through pop songcraft; Chris Thile went on to form Punch Brothers.

albums.label: Rounder
albums.description: Krauss's crystalline fiddle and vocal purity, paired with Union Station's tight, polished bluegrass picking (Dan Tyminski, Jerry Douglas), made this the crossover-friendly, radio-ready face of modern bluegrass. It is cleaner and more vocally driven than jam-leaning newgrass. It is for hearing bluegrass's most mainstream-capable ensemble at its most refined.
albums.lineage: A polished, vocal-forward continuation of first-generation bluegrass (R1), sitting opposite the jam-leaning newgrass of New Grass Revival and Billy Strings.
key_tracks: Let Me Touch You for a While

albums.label: Nonesuch
albums.description: Chris Thile's post-Nickel Creek project pushes bluegrass instrumentation toward classical-adjacent composition, anchored by the four-part suite 'The Blind Leaving the Blind,' which runs over 40 minutes across its movements. It treats mandolin, banjo, and fiddle as a chamber-music ensemble rather than a dance-tune string band. It is for listeners who want bluegrass technique pushed toward art-music ambition.
albums.lineage: Extends Nickel Creek's newgrass genre-blending toward classical composition and long-form suites, the most art-music-oriented branch of the bluegrass lineage that eventually feeds Billy Strings' and Molly Tuttle's more jam- and roots-rock-facing 2010s-2020s bluegrass.

albums.label: Rounder
albums.description: Strings's second solo album pairs blistering flatpicked guitar runs and jam-band-scaled improvisation with traditional bluegrass songwriting, drawing a younger, festival- and jam-scene audience into bluegrass. It is faster and more rock-adjacent in its soloing than Krauss's polished ensemble sound. It is for hearing bluegrass's 2010s-2020s jam-band crossover moment.
albums.lineage: Sounds like the clearest recent inheritor of New Grass Revival's improvisational newgrass, scaled to jam-band festival culture, alongside peers Molly Tuttle and Sierra Ferrell.

albums.label: ANTI-
albums.description: McCalla's fourth album, sung partly in Haitian Creole, pairs clawhammer banjo and cello with a narrative about Radio Haiti and her Haitian-American identity. Old-time string-band technique becomes a vehicle for a story far from the genre's usual Appalachian frame. It is for hearing old-time banjo tradition applied to a Haitian-American songwriting project.
albums.lineage: A former member of the Carolina Chocolate Drops, McCalla uses old-time banjo technique (R1) for Haitian-American and Creole storytelling, a culturally distinct branch of the tradition.

albums.label: Nonesuch
albums.description: Tuttle's first album with her band Golden Highway keeps virtuosic flatpicking guitar at its center, with banjo, mandolin and fiddle driving hard-picked string-band arrangements. She writes personally about growing up different and finding her own way. It is for hearing bluegrass at a current creative high point.
albums.lineage: A 2020s culmination of the newgrass lineage running from New Grass Revival through Nickel Creek, sounding like a peer of Billy Strings in the current bluegrass revival.

albums.label: Rounder
albums.description: A West Virginia-born songwriter blends bluegrass and old-time instrumentation with vintage country, gypsy-jazz, and folk textures. Her flexible, old-timey-inflected voice moves between wistful balladry and rowdy string-band numbers without settling into one lane. It is for hearing bluegrass and old-time tradition filtered through a genuinely idiosyncratic voice.
albums.lineage: A genre-blurring newgrass and old-time descendant that shares Molly Tuttle's and Billy Strings's bluegrass-revival moment while pulling in vintage pop and gypsy-jazz textures.
